title: Calculate weight and balance for an aircraft after an equipment change
subject: General
assumptions: Tare weight (chocks, jacks, ground locks) is subtracted from each scale reading before it is recorded.
Any location forward of the datum carries a negative arm value.
The datum used is the one published for the aircraft, taken from the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications.
The nose gear moment is negative, reflecting its arm forward of the datum.
Moment values are labeled in inch-pounds (in-lb) on the worksheet.
Any tare weight is subtracted from the scale readings before they are totaled.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

The task title says 'after an equipment change,' but the seven steps describe a scale weighing and CG computation with no added or removed equipment item. An SME must confirm whether the assessed deliverable is a weighing/EWCG calculation, an equipment-change (add/remove weight) calculation, or both.

The handbook page range (FAA-H-8083-30B 6-3 to 6-6) was located during compilation and is not cited by the procedure sheet. Every standard drawn from it — tare subtraction, unsummed arm column, rounding to tenths, TCDS maximum weight comparison — is provisional until an SME confirms the reference.
Is tare weight taught and assessed in this task at all? It appears nowhere in the procedure sheet's steps or notes.
Is rounding to tenths of an inch a graded requirement or merely the handbook's example precision?

Does the campus expect an actual aircraft weighing (scales, load cells) or a paper exercise with instructor-supplied weights? This decides whether the scale-indication photos and arm measurement are obtainable at all.

steps.text: Identify the weight at the landing gear locations.

checks.text: Three individual weights are recorded separately, each labeled to its gear position (RMLG, LMLG, NG).
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 1: read each scale for its individual weight; tricycle gear identified as RMLG, LMLG, NG.

checks.text: Each recorded value in pounds matches the indication on its corresponding scale or load cell.
checks.src: Step requires reading actual scale/load-cell indications, not estimated or carried-over figures.

checks.text: Tare weight (chocks, jacks, ground locks) is subtracted from each scale reading before it is recorded.
checks.src: "This extra weight is known as tare weight and must be subtracted from the scale reading." Handbook not cited by sheet; needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Scale readings recorded without subtracting tare weight, so all later moments and CG are inflated but look plausible.
Nose gear reading mislabeled or transposed with a main gear reading, giving a plausible but wrong CG.
A single combined total weight is recorded instead of three individual gear-position readings.

steps.text: Identify the arms of each weight.

checks.text: An arm is recorded for all three scale locations (RMLG, LMLG, NG), each expressed in inches.
checks.src: Note 2: 'The arm of each weight is its distance from the datum in inches'; example lists all three locations.

checks.text: Any location forward of the datum carries a negative arm value.
checks.src: Procedure note 2 gives '-45" NG'; handbook: 'Weight being added forward of the datum produces a negative moment (+weight, −arm).' Handbook is an uncited, provisional reference.

checks.text: The datum used is the one published for the aircraft, taken from the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications.
checks.src: 'This information is furnished by the FAA ... in the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications.' Uncited reference; needs subject-matter confirmation.

checks.text: Each recorded arm matches the actual distance from the datum to that gear/scale reaction point.
checks.src: Note 2 defines arm as distance from datum in inches, so the figure must be verified against a measured or published distance.

errors.text: Negative sign omitted on a forward-of-datum arm (e.g. nose gear entered as +45"), producing a plausible but wrong CG.
Arms measured from a convenient reference (firewall, spar, nose) rather than the published datum.
Arm values transcribed to the wrong location row, or units/labels omitted from the worksheet.

steps.text: Multiply the weight by the arm.

checks.text: Every weighed station row shows a moment equal to that row's own weight multiplied by that row's own arm.
checks.src: Sheet note 3: 'Multiply each weight by its own arm (e.g., 1,250 x 120 = 150,000... 1,125 x -45 = -50,625).'

checks.text: The nose gear moment is negative, reflecting its arm forward of the datum.
checks.src: Sheet shows -50,625; handbook: '+weight, −arm' gives 'a negative moment'. Handbook extract is uncited, so needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Each weight is paired with its own station's arm, with no arms swapped or reused between stations.
checks.src: Note 3 requires each weight be multiplied by 'its own arm'; three distinct station products expected.

checks.text: Moment values are labeled in inch-pounds (in-lb) on the worksheet.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Moment = Weight (arm) = 5 lb (80") = 400 in-lb'. Reference is uncited/assumed; requires SME confirmation.

checks.text: A moment entry is present for every station read on the scales, with no blank rows.
checks.src: Note 1 identifies three weighing locations; note 3 requires a product for each.

errors.text: Negative sign dropped on the forward (nose gear) moment, so a plausible-looking but falsely aft CG results.
A weight is multiplied by another station's arm, or the main-gear arm is applied to the nose gear.
Moments recorded without units or with inconsistent rounding between rows.

checks.text: The worksheet shows all three individual scale weights listed and a single total-weight entry labeled in pounds.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 4 sums the three readings to one value expressed in LBS (e.g., 3,575 LBS).

checks.text: The recorded total equals the arithmetic sum of the left main, right main, and nose gear readings.
checks.src: Handbook: "the weights need to be summed" and "the weight and moment columns are summed"; procedure note 4 gives the same addition.

checks.text: Any tare weight is subtracted from the scale readings before they are totaled.
checks.src: "This extra weight is known as tare weight and must be subtracted from the scale reading." Provisional: handbook not cited by procedure sheet; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The total weight is checked against the maximum allowable gross weight from the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications.
checks.src: "maximum authorized weight of the aircraft and its contents, and is indicated in the Aircraft Specifications or TCDS." Provisional: uncited handbook, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Tare weight (chocks, jacks, ground locks) left in the readings, giving a plausible but overstated total weight.
A scale reading omitted or transposed, or moments added instead of weights, so the total is wrong.
Total entered without units or illegibly, or arm signs mistakenly applied to the weight column.

checks.text: The total moment equals the algebraic sum of the individual moments, with forward-of-datum moments subtracted (e.g., 243,375 in-lb).
checks.src: Handbook: "The weight and moment columns are summed"; signs per "Weight being added forward of the datum produces a negative moment". Assumed reference needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Only the weight and moment columns are totaled; the arm column carries no sum.
checks.src: Handbook: "The arm column is not summed." Uncited reference located at compilation; requires subject-matter confirmation.

checks.text: The total moment is recorded with its sign and in inch-pounds, matching the moments carried from step 3.
checks.src: Handbook shows "Moment = 400 in-lb" and moment sign table (Figure 6-3). Provisional: handbook not cited by the procedure sheet.

errors.text: Nose-gear (negative) moment added as a positive value, inflating the total moment while the worksheet still looks complete.
Individual moment omitted or mistranscribed from step 3, so the total does not reconcile with the listed moments.
Total moment written without units or sign, or arm column mistakenly totaled.

steps.text: Divide the total moment by the total weight.

checks.text: The quotient equals total moment divided by total weight and matches an independent recomputation of the recorded figures.
checks.src: Procedure step 6 (243,375 / 3,575 = 68.07"); handbook: "the CG being equal to the total moment divided by the total weight".

checks.text: The result is recorded as a CG station in inches referenced to the datum, with correct sign if forward of datum.
checks.src: Note 6 records the answer as 68.07" CG; note 2 establishes negative arms forward of datum.

checks.text: No total is entered for the arm column; the CG value alone occupies the bottom of that column.
checks.src: "The arm column is not summed. The number appearing at the bottom of that column is the CG." Uncited extract; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The CG figure is rounded to tenths of an inch on the worksheet.
checks.src: "106.9" (106.87 rounded to tenths)". Uncited extract, provisional; procedure sheet uses hundredths, so SME must confirm.

errors.text: Division inverted (total weight ÷ total moment), producing a small plausible-looking number instead of a CG station.
Divided by an incomplete weight total (e.g., mains only, nose gear omitted), giving a CG that appears in range.
CG recorded without units or datum sign convention, or arm column erroneously summed.

steps.text: Determine if the CG is in range.

checks.text: The CG limits used are recorded with their source (TCDS entry or instructor-given value) for this specific aircraft model/serial.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "CG range is found on the TCDS or a given value"; handbook: data "furnished by the FAA ... in the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications".

checks.text: The computed CG in inches from datum falls within the stated forward and aft limits (e.g., 68.07" within 64"–70").
checks.src: Procedure sheet Note 7 example: "If the CG range is 64"-70" ... then the CG is within range"; handbook gives no numeric limits.

checks.text: The worksheet records an explicit in-range or out-of-range determination, not just a bare CG number.
checks.src: Step 7 requires a determination as the deliverable of the calculation.

checks.text: Total weight from step 4 is also compared against the maximum allowable gross weight from the TCDS.
checks.src: "maximum authorized weight of the aircraft and its contents, and is indicated in the Aircraft Specifications or TCDS"; assumed reference, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: CG declared in range against a remembered or wrong-model CG range instead of the aircraft's TCDS limits.
Nose gear negative arm mishandled upstream, giving a plausible-looking CG that is falsely inside limits.
CG value computed but no in-range/out-of-range conclusion or limits recorded on the worksheet.
Units or datum reference omitted, or CG rounded inconsistently with the worked example.
